inline_comments.comment:
This type-only import creates a cross-package coupling between `code/core` (core-server) and the React renderer package. Even though it's `import type` (no runtime dep), it means `core-server` now depends on a React-specific internal type path deep inside the renderer. If `componentMetaExtractor.ts` is restructured or its export names change, this core file silently breaks.

Consider instead either: (a) defining a shared `ComponentDoc` interface in `storybook/internal/types` or a new shared manifest types module, or (b) duplicating a minimal interface locally in this file with a comment referencing the source of truth. The existing approach violates the architecture principle that `core` should not import renderer-specific internals.

The JSDoc comment says **"1 = outermost JSX element"** but the implementation in `getComponentImports.ts` computes `depth = jsxDepth - 1`, where `jsxDepth` is already incremented by `JSXElement.enter` before `JSXOpeningElement` fires. So the outermost top-level element gets `depth = 0`, not `1`.

This is confirmed by `findMatchingComponent` in `generator.ts` which treats `jsxDepth === 0` as the top-level sentinel:
```typescript
if (cur.jsxDepth === 0) {
  return cur; // Cannot be shallower
}
```
The JSDoc should read: `/** Minimum JSX nesting depth ... (0 = outermost JSX element). */`

When `fs.watch` with `{ recursive: true }` fails (e.g., on Linux kernels < 5.x or Node.js < 22), the error is logged only at `logger.debug` level — essentially invisible to the user in a default Storybook setup. The consequence is that all file watching is silently disabled, so component prop changes won't be reflected until a full restart.

This should be at least `logger.warn` with a message explaining the degraded behavior, e.g.:
```
[reactComponentMeta] Failed to watch directory (file watching disabled — incremental prop updates unavailable): ${err}
```
Alternatively, document in the feature docs that recursive watch on Linux requires Node.js ≥ 22.

The preset type signature declares `{ manifestEntries: IndexEntry[]; watch: boolean }` (non-optional `boolean`), but `writeManifests` calls `getManifests(presets)` without a `watch` argument, so `watch` defaults to `undefined`. This value propagates to `presets.apply('experimental_manifests', undefined, { manifestEntries, watch: undefined })` and is destructured in `manifests()` as `boolean` (the declared type), creating a runtime/type mismatch.

The runtime behavior happens to be correct (`undefined` is falsy → non-watch path), but the type contract is violated. Change the preset options type to `{ manifestEntries: IndexEntry[]; watch?: boolean }` and update `createComponentMetaManager(watch: boolean | undefined)` accordingly to make the intent explicit.

The old `vitest.setup.ts` used `vi.resetAllMocks()`, which clears both call history AND resets mock implementations to their defaults. The new `setupMemfsMocks()` uses `vi.clearAllMocks()`, which only clears call history but leaves implementations intact from a previous test's `mockImplementation` call.

Since the setup explicitly re-applies all mock implementations immediately after, this is usually equivalent in practice. However, any mock that was set outside of `setupMemfsMocks()` (e.g., a spy set up inside an individual test's `beforeEach`) will retain its implementation across tests. This is a subtle behavioral difference that could cause test pollution. Consider using `vi.resetAllMocks()` to match the original behavior.

general_comments.comment:
**`fs.watch` with `recursive: true` is not supported on Linux (Node.js < 22).**

The `watchDirectory` method in `ComponentMetaManager` uses `watch(dir, { recursive: true }, ...)`. On Linux with Node.js versions before 22.5.0, `fs.watch` with `recursive: true` throws `Error: ENOSYS: function not implemented`. While the error is caught and logged at `logger.debug`, the practical effect is that *no directories are watched at all* on most CI environments and Linux development machines.

This means the main value proposition of the new `react-component-meta` engine in dev mode — incremental updates without full restarts — silently does not work on Linux. At minimum, surface a `logger.warn` after the first watch failure. A longer-term fix would be to use a cross-platform recursive watcher library (e.g., `chokidar`, which is already available in the monorepo) or to polyfill recursive watching with multiple shallow `fs.watch` calls on Linux.

**`vitest.setup.ts` gutted; mocks now opt-in per test file — risks inconsistent setups.**

The previous `vitest.setup.ts` established a guaranteed, consistent environment for all tests in the renderer: memfs mocking, `cachedResolveImport` override, `loadConfig` stub, etc. These were applied globally in `beforeEach`. The new approach moves all of this into `setupMemfsMocks()` and requires each test file to call it explicitly.

This is fragile: a new test file that imports `getComponents` or `manifests` without calling `setupMemfsMocks()` will inadvertently hit the real filesystem, produce non-deterministic results, or fail with import resolution errors. The `ComponentMetaManager.test.ts` and `ComponentMetaProject.*.test.ts` files intentionally use real filesystem (temp dirs) — but the `generator.test.ts` and `getComponentImports.test.ts` files now silently depend on remembering to call `setupMemfsMocks()`. Consider re-establishing a global setup that applies only to the memfs-based tests (e.g., via a separate `vitest.config` project or a tagged test group) to make the boundary explicit.

**`getComponents` signature change from sync to async is a breaking API change without documentation.**

`getComponents` was previously synchronous and is now `async`, returning `Promise<ComponentRef[]>`. `getComponentData` similarly became `async`. These are exported functions (or at least internally used across multiple callers). The change cascades through `generator.ts`, `getComponentImports.test.ts`, and related test files. While the diff updates all known callers, this is a breaking change for any third-party addons or internal consumers that cached a synchronous call. The function signatures (and the `getComponentData` public export) should have corresponding changelog or deprecation notices given that `getComponentData` is marked `@public`.
